exec_summary.bullet: **Trade credit stress record:** The Slovak trade credit gap widened to +18.1pp from -1.7pp in the prior wave, leaving Slovakia more stressed than the EA's +10.7pp.
**Rate tightening eased:** A net 31.8% of Slovak firms reported tighter interest rates, down 12 pp from a net 43.8%, while the EA rose 8.2 pp to a net 48.2%.
**Bank willingness improved:** A net 18.3% of Slovak firms reported improved bank willingness to lend, up 10.5 pp from a net 7.8% and outpacing the EA's net 5.4%.
**Profitability recovered:** A net 16% of Slovak firms reported falling profits, improving 18 pp from a net 34% decline and outperforming the EA's net 21% deterioration.

sections.title: Changes in Terms and Conditions of Bank Financing (Q10)
sections.finding: Slovak interest rate tightening eased 12 pp as EA pressures intensified
bullets: A net 31.8% of Slovak firms (n=58) reported tighter interest rates, down 12 pp from a net 43.8% in the previous wave — while the EA rose 8.2 pp to a net 48.2% (n=1,962).
A net 10.5% of Slovak firms (n=58) reported reduced loan or credit line availability, easing marginally by 1.9 pp from the previous wave's net 12.4%, remaining above the EA's net 7.0%.
EA collateral requirements tightened to a net 13.2% (n=1,992) and other terms to a net 17.8% (n=1,964), both rising from their previous-wave levels.

chart.question_caption: Did your bank loan terms improve, stay the same or worsen?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak interest rate tightening fell to net 31.8% in wave 40.

sections.title: Financing Need vs Availability Gap (Q5/Q9)
sections.finding: Slovak bank loan and credit line stress reversed sharply as trade credit tightened
bullets: The Slovak trade credit gap widened to +18.1pp (n=102) from -1.7pp in the previous wave, as need rose to +12.5pp and availability fell to -5.6pp, leaving Slovakia more stressed than the EA's +10.7pp.

The Slovak credit line gap improved from +15.3pp to -11.2pp (n=212), as need eased to +2.7pp and availability rose to +13.9pp, reversing from above the EA's prior +14.0pp to below its current +16.4pp.

chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak trade credit gap widened to +18.1pp in wave 40.

sections.title: Bank Loan Applications and Access Conditions (Q7A/Q7B)
sections.finding: Slovak firms' bank credit access gap more than doubled the euro area rate
bullets: A net 10.21% of Slovak firms (n=104) seeking bank loans were either discouraged from applying or turned down in wave 40, more than double the EA’s 4.67% (n=3,622).

chart.question_caption: Did you apply for financing in the last quarter?
chart.chart_subtitle: 10.21% of Slovak firms were discouraged or rejected for bank loans.

sections.title: Expected Availability of External Financing (Q23)
sections.finding: Slovak firms' bank loan availability expectations turned positive, diverging from EA
bullets: A net 2% of Slovak firms (n=87) expected bank loan availability to improve in wave 40, reversing from a net 6% expecting deterioration in wave 39, while EA expectations deteriorated to a net 8%.
Slovak firms' credit line expectations rose 11 pp to a net 7% expecting improvement (n=102), compared with a net 4% of EA firms expecting deterioration — an 11 pp SK–EA gap.
Trade credit expectations for Slovak firms held at a net 6% expecting deterioration (n=53), broadly unchanged from wave 39's net 6%.

chart.question_caption: Do you expect financing to get easier or harder in the next few months?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak firms expect bank loan availability to improve at net 2%.

sections.title: Purpose of Financing (Q6A)
sections.finding: Slovak firms shifted toward refinancing as fixed investment financing fell
bullets: Refinancing or paying off obligations was cited by 21.1% of Slovak firms (n=192), rising 4.1 pp from 17.0% in the previous wave and exceeding the EA rate of 15.9%.
Fixed investment financing fell from 40.7% to 34.1% among Slovak firms (n=191), placing Slovakia 5.3 pp below the EA's 39.4% — a reversal from the prior wave when SK exceeded the EA.
Inventory and working capital remained the dominant financing purpose for Slovak firms at 55.8% (n=193), 15.1 pp above the EA's 40.7%, easing 1.2 pp from 57.0% in the previous wave.

chart.question_caption: What did your firm use financing for this quarter?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak firms cited refinancing at 21.1%, up 4.1 pp.

sections.title: Factors Affecting Access to External Financing (Q11)
sections.finding: Bank willingness to lend improved notably for Slovak firms in wave 40
bullets: A net 18.3% of Slovak firms (n=236) reported improved bank willingness to provide credit, rising 10.5 pp from a net 7.8% in the previous wave and outpacing the EA's net 5.4%.
Slovak firms' (n=370) perception of the general economic outlook improved by 8.1 pp to a net 43.5% reporting deterioration, while the EA worsened by 2.4 pp to a net 31.8%.
Access to public financial support deteriorated for a net 25.1% of Slovak firms (n=318), worsening 3.9 pp from the previous wave's net 21.2%, and remaining below the EA's net 17.3%.

chart.question_caption: How have these factors changed this quarter?
chart.chart_subtitle: Net 18.3% of Slovak firms reported improved bank lending willingness.

sections.title: Business Situation Indicators (Q2)
sections.finding: Slovak firms' profitability improved sharply as cost pressures eased in wave 40
bullets: A net 16% of Slovak firms (n=194) reported falling profits, improving by 18 pp from the net 34% decline in the previous wave — outperforming the EA's net 21% deterioration.
Slovak turnover remained negative at a net 5% of firms (n=194), improving by 8 pp from the prior wave's net 13%, while the EA posted a positive net 4%.
Labour cost pressures eased by 19 pp to a net 59% of Slovak firms (n=194) reporting increases, converging with the EA's net 56% after exceeding it by 20 pp in wave 39.

chart.question_caption: Did your firm's indicators change this quarter?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak profit losses narrowed to a net 16% in wave 40.

sections.title: Expected Changes in Turnover and Investment (Q26)
sections.finding: Slovak turnover outlook recovered sharply, but investment expectations fell
bullets: Slovak firms' turnover expectations rose to a net 21% (n=243), up 14 pp from the net 7% recorded two quarters earlier, though still trailing the EA's net 25%.
Fixed investment expectations declined from a net 15% to a net 9% in Slovakia (n=243), while the EA's improved from a net 9% to a net 14% — reversing their relative positions.
The SK–EA turnover expectations gap narrowed to 4 pp in wave 40, down from nearly 19 pp two quarters earlier, reflecting a convergence in near-term business confidence.

chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak turnover outlook rose to a net 21% in wave 40.

sections.title: Price, Wage and Employment Expectations (Q31/Q34)
sections.finding: Slovak firms face margin compression as input costs outpace selling price expectations
bullets: Slovak firms (n=397) expected production input prices to rise 7.91% over the next 12 months, outpacing selling price expectations of 5.29% (n=394), pointing to margin compression.
Average selling price expectations rose from +3.75% (wave 39) to +5.29% (wave 40) for Slovak firms, remaining below the EA's +7.15% (n=11,832).

Slovak firms anticipated 5.00% wage growth (n=398), above the EA's 4.76%, while 12-month inflation expectations held at +4.87% (n=164), rising only marginally by 0.19 pp versus the EA's 2.28 pp jump to +6.16%.

chart.question_caption: How much do you expect inflation to rise or fall next year?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak firms expect 5.29% selling price rise, below EA 7.15%.

sections.title: Inflation Risk Outlook (Q33)
sections.finding: Slovak firms see stronger upside inflation risk than euro area peers
bullets: A net 62.25% of Slovak firms (n=194) saw upside risks to five-year inflation, exceeding the euro area's net 55.37% (n=4,881) by 6.9 pp, consistent with local price persistence.
The Slovak upside inflation risk balance rose marginally from a net 61.23% in the previous wave, with the euro area also ticking up from net 54.04%.
German firms moved in the opposite direction, with the upside inflation risk balance easing by 2.25 pp to a net 49.08%, below both Slovakia and the euro area.

chart.question_caption: What’s the biggest inflation risk in five years?
chart.chart_subtitle: Net 62.25% of Slovak firms see upside inflation risks.

sections.title: Most Pressing Business Problems (Q0B)
sections.finding: Production costs and skilled staff top Slovak firms' business pressures
bullets: Costs of production or labour scored 6.11/10 for Slovak firms (n=194) — the most pressing named problem among the seven tested — easing from 6.62 in the previous wave, compared with the EA's 6.73/10.

Availability of skilled staff or experienced managers scored 5.97/10 (n=193), the second most pressing named problem, falling from 6.64 in the previous wave, yet still below the EA average of 6.70/10.
Finding customers rose to 5.38/10 (n=192) from 5.24 in the previous wave, ranking third among named problems for Slovak firms, though remaining below the EA score of 6.09/10.

chart.question_caption: How important were these problems for your firm?
chart.chart_subtitle: Slovak firms score production costs at 6.11/10.
